title: Dominic and the Glasshouse
premise: Ansel Ravensworth, a night librarian in a city that never quite sleeps, learns that the glasshouse where she grew up — and the sentence her late mother painted across its panes in a language no one could read — will be auctioned and demolished. As she fights to save it, she collides with Dominic Ferro, the estranged foster brother who once lived there with her, now the auctioneer's appraiser. Translating the sentence forces them to excavate the truth of who abandoned whom, and to admit that the glasshouse was never a home so much as the people inside it. On demolition day, Ansel reads the translated sentence aloud — 'Stay, even when you leave' — and chooses to build a found family with Dominic rather than mourn a building.
about_author: Silas Villalobos is a former greenhouse keeper turned archivist who writes about the architecture of belonging. He lives above a shuttered botanical garden, where he keeps one pane of old glass on his windowsill as a paperweight.

chapters.title: The Hours Between Streetlights
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. We meet her shelving books at 3 a.m., cataloging other people's lives while avoiding her own; a patron returns a book about glasshouses, triggering a memory she suppresses. Emotional beat: quiet loneliness disguised as routine.

chapters.title: Lot 47
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. An auction flyer names the Ravensworth glasshouse for sale, demolition pending. She visits the fenced lot at dawn and finds Dominic Ferro measuring the panes for the appraiser — the boy her mother took in, gone fifteen years. Beat: shock curdling into resentment.

chapters.title: What the Panes Remember
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. He reveals he was hired to inventory the property, not destroy it, and admits he came back looking for her. A tense walk through the overgrown interior surfaces shared memories of their mother-figure, Marisol. Beat: reluctant tenderness.

chapters.title: A Sentence in No Language
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. She photographs the painted sentence and takes it to linguists, who fail; an old neighbor suggests it may be invented — a private language Marisol made from fragments of everyone she loved. Beat: grief reframed as inheritance.

chapters.title: The Auctioneer's Ledger
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. His employer pressures him to finalize the appraisal fast; he discovers the ledger shows Ansel's name still on a childhood guardianship record Marisol filed — proof she intended to keep them both. Beat: guilt over his long silence.

chapters.title: Tenants
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. She confronts Dominic: he left without goodbye after Marisol's death, and she has spent years feeling unchosen. He counters that she never wrote either. The fight cracks something open. Beat: raw accusation, mutual wound exposed.

chapters.title: Fragments of Everyone
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Decoding the sentence together, they realize each word comes from a different person Marisol sheltered — including words from each of them. The sentence isn't translatable alone; it requires both their memories. Beat: collaboration as reconciliation.

chapters.title: Demolition Notice
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. The date moves up; his firm threatens to fire him if he stalls. He must choose between the job that brought him back and the family he's rebuilding. He leaks the delay paperwork to buy time. Beat: sacrifice, rising stakes.

chapters.title: The Last Night in Glass
chapters.summary: Climax, alternating POV. On the eve of demolition, Ansel and Dominic hold a vigil among the panes, reading the finished translation aloud: 'Stay, even when you leave.' Neighbors, patrons, and strangers Marisol once sheltered arrive, drawn by word of mouth. Beat: catharsis and communal belonging.

chapters.title: Owner, Not Tenant
chapters.summary: Resolution, Ansel's POV. The glasshouse falls, but the salvaged panes become a community reading room Ansel and Dominic co-found; she signs the lease as owner. She finally feels like an author of her own life rather than a caretaker of others'. Beat: earned peace, open future.
